subject: Escalation: Request for multi-year price locks & renewal protection — Atlas Data
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: multi-year price locks + renewal protection for Atlas (ATLD-2026-042)

Team —

Quick summary: Atlas Data is asking for a 3-year commitment with an explicit price lock for year 1 & 2 (no more than 5% uplift in year 3), plus a renewal protection clause that preserves current seat-based pricing on renewal for up to 12 months after the term in exchange for a 20% upfront commitment discount. They want redlines in the MPA this week.

Why this matters: Atlas is a strategic analytics partner in our target segment. Losing momentum here would likely push them to a competitor offering aggressive enterprise discounts. We have an active POC and they committed to pilot success metrics — high probability to expand.

Ask: I need an approval path for: (1) a limited 20% multi-year discount tied to a signed 3-year MPA, (2) a firm price-lock schedule with an uplift cap of 5% in year 3, (3) a renewal-protection clause that prevents >10% price increases on the immediate renewal if we maintain agreed SLA/usage thresholds, and (4) guidance on whether we can accept Atlas’ requested language around carry-forward credits.

Attachments: redwood-draft-mpa-2026.pdf (draft with proposed redlines), atlas-requested-terms-summary.xlsx

I’ve copied Legal (Dev) and Finance (Marissa). Laura/Rishi — what level of exec approval do we need to sign this week if Legal signs off on the wording?

Thanks,
Markus
Head of Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: multi-year price locks + renewal protection for Atlas (ATLD-2026-042)

Markus —

Reviewed the draft. High-level legal take: the price-lock + 5% uplift cap is acceptable if we limit the clause to the specific SKU/usage band used in the pilot and include a materiality threshold (e.g., >15% usage change invalidates the cap). Renewal-protection as requested is unusual but we can offer a one-time renewal protection window (12 months) tied to a renewal notice period and a defined SLA/usage covenant.

Two legal asks before we go to execs:
- Narrow the carry-forward credit language so credits expire after 9 months (Atlas requested 24 months).
- Add a clause preserving our right to adjust net unit pricing for commodity/infra cost spikes linked to public cloud region outages (we can cap those adjustments at 7% with 30 days’ notice).

If Finance signs off on the discount economics, I think Legal can support routing to Rishi for commercial sign-off.

—Dev
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: multi-year price locks + renewal protection for Atlas (ATLD-2026-042)

Team —

Finance perspective: the 20% upfront/3-year commit is reasonable if we secure non-cancellable minimums and a payment cadence that includes 50% upfront. We modeled the uplift cap and renewal protection — worst-case NPV impact vs. list is within acceptable thresholds for a strategic account, provided we include:

- Minimum annual commitment floors (to avoid low adoption risk)
- Termination for convenience fee if Atlas exits before year 2 (to recover implementation & discount delta)
- Clear reconciliation timings for carry-forward credits (9 months expiry recommended)

If Legal implements Dev’s suggested limits, Finance is ok to recommend commercial approval. Rishi, happy to provide a one-page summary for exec review.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Finance

I reviewed Dev and Marissa’s notes. Approve escalation to Execs with the following firm boundaries:

- 20% max discount for a 3-year MPA when paired with 50% upfront payment and minimum annual commitment floors.
- Price-lock: no increases in years 1 & 2; year 3 capped at +5% over year 2.
- Renewal protection: one 12-month protection window post-term limited to <=10% increase and contingent on meeting SLA/usage covenants.
- Carry-forward credits capped at 9 months and subject to reconciliation.
- Any infra-linked pricing adjustments capped at 7% require CEO sign-off.

Markus — assemble the one-pager, clean MPA, and finance memo. I will submit the packet to the Exec Approval queue and flag for Nilou and Tom. If they sign off, Legal can finalize the redlines and we can return to Atlas with DocuSign-ready MPA.
